hook: SCP-348 is a small ceramic bowl that fills with soup whenever someone nearby is a little bit sick. That is nearly the whole premise, and it is enough. Read it slowly; the test logs are short, and each entry is a tiny story of its own.
whyItMatters: It is a Safe object with no danger at all, and the file never explains where the bowl came from; the only hint is the Chinese phrase for thinking of you etched on its side. Everything else is data that the reader turns into feeling. Telling a whole family relationship through one line of background and one line of result is the technique that carries the page.
thingsToNotice:
The child logs work like flash fiction: a boy who argues with his parents is told not to forget to brush, a boy whose parents divorced gets an apology addressed to a son, and a girl whose father died in a car crash reads that she is loved. With adults the bowl grows stingy and the words come out worn and faded: a woman who turned down her father's help gets a bare one-word question, and a daughter who supported estranged parents finds the soup bitter at first but is thanked after her father's recent death.

The sharpest entry is the man who murdered his father a year earlier: he refuses the soup, gets a stomachache, and once it is poured out the bowl fills with what looks like salt water for three hours, like tears. The researchers admit they cannot tell whether the messages come from the subjects' fathers or from the bowl itself, and the last addendum ends with a dying grandfather calling it the best soup he ever tasted and passing peacefully a week later.
